problem: Semantic navigation with LLMs has relied on large, cloud-hosted, high-parameter models, which are costly and impractical for on-robot or consumer-hardware use; it is unclear how small quantized local LLMs/VLMs perform.
motivation: Running LLMs/VLMs locally on a consumer-grade laptop would make semantic navigation practical for robots without cloud dependence. The paper checks whether small quantized models can extract semantic knowledge (room type, goal room) sufficient to build an executable path in simulation.
key_idea: Evaluate low-parameter (<=8.54B) quantized local LLMs and VLMs on room classification from object lists and goal selection, and combine LLMs with VLMs (used for hard scenes where no object list can be extracted).
insight: Based on the abstract only: Llama3 is the most accurate room classifier among the tested LLMs, while goal-selection performance varies by room and by LLM. VLMs are best reserved for hard-to-classify scenes where an object list cannot be extracted, so combining both model types exploits their complementary strengths.
method: Room classification: small quantized LLMs (Gemma, Llama3, two Mistral quantizations) classify rooms from lists of detected objects, compared against an SVC baseline.
Goal selection: LLMs choose which room/object satisfies a human-set goal, with performance analysed per room and per LLM.
VLM evaluation: 4-bit and un-quantized Chameleon and un-quantized Moondream2 classify scenes directly from images.
Combined approach: LLM route when an object list is available; VLM fallback for hard-to-classify scenes.
Evaluation framework: simple framework for testing VLMs and LLMs in semantic navigation, generating executable paths in a simulated environment.

setting.backbone: Gemma, Llama3, Mistral (two quantizations) LLMs; Chameleon (4-bit and full), Moondream2 VLMs; SVC baseline
setting.training_data: none (pretrained models used as-is; SVC trained on task data, details not given in abstract)
setting.observation: object lists extracted from the environment and images of scenes
setting.action_space: executable path generated from semantic knowledge (details not given)

results: Llama3 is the most accurate room classifier among the four tested LLMs; goal-selection accuracy varies across rooms and LLMs. VLMs help most on hard scenes where objects cannot be listed. No numeric results are available from the abstract.
limitations: Evaluation is in simulation only, with no real-robot experiments stated.
Only small models were studied and compared with an SVC; no standard navigation benchmarks were reported.
